title: be: I am / You are / She is
objective: Build affirmative statements about yourself and others with the correct form of be: am, are, is.
intro_md:
[L1: In this lesson you build sentences with am, are and is: I am a student. You are new. She is my teacher. English always needs these small words — you cannot leave them out.]
{{l1_contrast:copula_be}}
notes: TODO_audio: ex2 (She is a teacher., 0.75x), ex7 (We are students., 1.0x), ex9 speaking model prompt. Band map §15: L07 vocab=4, grammar G1+G3. All four items are in band file §4 U1 sample list (items 12, 13, 14, 43).

exercises.rationale: Form-meaning link for the four predicate words before any grammar work: every be-sentence in this lesson ends in one of them.

exercises.prompt: [audio, 0.75x] 'She is a teacher.' — [L1: What exactly did you hear?]
exercises.rationale: Perception before production: zero-copula L1 speakers (ar/zh/vi) must first HEAR the unstressed is to stop deleting it.

options.label: She is a teacher.
options.rationale: is links she and teacher; it is short and unstressed but always there.

options.label: She a teacher.
options.rationale: Zero-copula transfer (ar/zh/vi): the learner's L1 pattern without be — trains noticing the missing is.

options.label: She are a teacher.
options.rationale: Agreement error: catches learners who hear that a be-word is present but not which one.

exercises.prompt: [L1: Match each person word to the correct ending.]
exercises.rationale: The three-way am/are/is choice by subject is the core of G1+G3; matching isolates the agreement decision with no other load.

exercises.prompt: I ___ a student. My teacher ___ from Mexico.
exercises.rationale: am vs is with a noun subject (my teacher), not just a pronoun; 'be' in the bank catches learners who learned the dictionary form and use it uninflected ('I be').
Adjective-before-noun order inside a be-sentence: predicted es/pt transfer is 'a student new' (noun-adjective order); feedback names the adjective position.

exercises.prompt: My teacher is Ana. ___ is from Brazil.
exercises.rationale: English subject pronouns are obligatory: es speakers drop them ('Es de Brasil' → 'Is from Brazil'); 'Her' catches possessive-for-subject confusion.

exercises.prompt: [audio, 1.0x] 'We are students.' — [L1: What exactly did you hear?]
exercises.rationale: Extends agreement to we + are and exposes the plural -s on students in connected speech (final-s deletion preview for vi/zh).

options.label: We are students.
options.rationale: are with we, and a final -s on students — both are easy to miss at natural speed.

options.label: We are student.
options.rationale: Misses the plural -s: the exact segment vi/zh speakers tend to delete when listening and speaking.

options.label: I am a student.
options.rationale: Person confusion: catches learners matching the familiar chunk instead of the subject they heard.

exercises.rationale: Spanish drops the subject pronoun (Somos…); the English answer forces the learner to supply we — the single highest-value es-to-en habit change for be.

exercises.prompt: [L1: Say who you are: your name and what you are — student or teacher.]
asr_focus: presence of 'm in I'm (copula — ar/zh/vi zero-copula contrast)
article a before the role noun
exercises.rationale: Personalized production of G1; ASR checks the contracted copula, the #1 predicted omission for zero-copula L1s.

exercises.prompt: [L1: Introduce yourself and one classmate to the AI: give both names, say what each of you is (student or teacher), and where each of you is from.]
exercises.rationale: Forces all three forms (I am / she is / we are) in one real exchange; integrates L03 name chunks and L05 origin chunks; counts toward guided-interaction minutes.
